definition: Relational world refers to a way of understanding social life as created through relationships, shared presence, care, and mutual accountability. In this sense, people make a meaningful world together through collective practices that build belonging, community, and responsibility toward one another and their environment.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly support the definition’s first clause: “a way of understanding social life as created through relationships” (the packet describes skateboarding practices and what they demonstrate, but does not provide a general definitional account of how to understand social life).

While the packet mentions care, shared presence, community building, belonging, and accountability/solidarity, it does not explicitly support the definition’s broader, generalized phrasing that “mutual accountability” is part of the meaning of “relational world” (accountability is present in the paper’s framing of practices, but not stated as a definitional component of the term).

The definition states that “people make a meaningful world together” and “build belonging, community, and responsibility toward one another and their environment,” but the packet supports these elements specifically for “Nairobi’s skateboarders” and their practices, not as the general meaning of the term independent of that context.
